# Overview

GX helps teams understand and review AI-written code without treating every pull request as an isolated diff.

The open-source `gx` CLI captures coding sessions, records staged changes as reviewable revisions inside stacks, and publishes those stacks as normal Git branches and commits. The paid GitHub features add [PR Summaries and `@gx` chat](/docs/github) inside GitHub pull requests.

## Start here

- [Get started](/docs/getting-started): install GX, sign in, and publish your first revision.
- [How it works](/docs/how-it-works): why GX stores more context than Git, and what stacks and revisions are.
- [CLI](/docs/cli): every command with flags, examples, and exit codes.
- [MCP setup](/docs/mcp): let coding agents commit, inspect, review, and push through MCP tools.
- [Pull Requests](/docs/github): PR Summaries, `@gx` chat, and paid GitHub review features.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting): common errors and how to fix them.

## Core workflow

GX keeps the Git staging mental model: `git add` chooses the scope, and `gx commit` replaces `git commit`.

```bash
git add <files>                        # choose the scope of the revision
gx commit -m "describe this revision"  # record it as a GX revision
gx status                              # inspect stacks before publishing (alias: gxs)
git push                               # the GX pre-push hook publishes sessions + metadata
```

A first commit looks like this:

```text
$ git add src/retry.js
$ gx commit -m "add retry helper with attempt limit"

Revision recorded
Message       add retry helper with attempt limit
Revision      qltmnmynnyzk
Commit        b694d3be
Stack         main
Provenance    absent
```

Every `gx commit` produces a normal Git commit (`b694d3be` above) plus a GX **revision** (`qltmnmynnyzk`) that stays editable and carries review context: which captured session produced it, what the agent reported doing, and where it sits in its stack. `Provenance` shows whether a captured coding session was linked to the revision — `absent` here because no agent session was running.

The CLI installer also adds two shortcuts:

```bash
gxs   # gx status
gxr   # gx review
```

For a large messy working copy, the advanced bulk organizer can split the work into smaller revisions automatically:

```bash
gx generate   # hidden from gx --help; see CLI → Bulk organize
gx status
gx push
```

## Product model

GX uses a few terms consistently:

- **Session**: captured coding context from an agent, editor, or shell.
- **Revision**: one reviewable logical change, including the code diff and the context that explains how it was produced.
- **Stack** (also called a **feature** in status output): an ordered line of revisions that should be reviewed together.
- **Review bundle**: the published payload that joins code changes, sessions, metadata, and review evidence.

GX still outputs normal Git branches, commits, and pull requests. The GX terms describe the product model before it is exported to Git.

A Git commit is a durable snapshot plus a short message. That is still useful, but it is often too thin for AI-generated work: the commit does not know which agent session produced it, which prompt or shell commands mattered, whether the change was split out of a larger messy workspace, or how it relates to nearby generated work.

A GX revision is the review unit. It can become a Git commit, but it carries richer review context around that commit: session provenance, generated summary, file-level intent, and its position in the stack. Calling it a revision keeps the focus on reviewable evolution of the work, not only on the final Git object.

A Git branch is a pointer in a repository. A GX stack is the product shape of the work: ordered revisions, their dependencies, and the context needed to understand them. GX exports stacks to branches because GitHub and Git still expect branches, but agents and reviewers work better with stacks because they can see the sequence of intent instead of only the final branch state.

# Get started

Start with GX when you want coding agents to produce reviewable work instead of one large undifferentiated diff.

The usual path is:

1. Install the CLI.
2. Sign in with GitHub.
3. Initialize GX in a repository.
4. Stage, commit with GX, inspect, and push.

## Install

The CLI runs on macOS and Linux (arm64 / amd64):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, run GX inside WSL. You can request a native Windows build from the [download page](/download).

The installer places four binaries in `~/.local/bin`:

| Binary | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `gx` | the CLI |
| `gx-mcp` | stdio MCP server for coding agents ([MCP setup](/docs/mcp)) |
| `gxs` | shortcut for `gx status` |
| `gxr` | shortcut for `gx review` |

Verify the install:

```bash
gx version   # prints the installed version
gx doctor    # checks capture, hooks, and workflow state
```

## Sign in

GX uses GitHub for identity. Cloud sign-in is required to push metadata and use GX code review.

```bash
gx auth login
gx auth status
```

The web app sign-in and CLI sign-in are linked through your GitHub account. After signing in from the CLI, you can see signed-in CLI devices in the web app, including machine name, GX version, last-used time, and session expiry. Pass `--name` to control how the machine appears there:

```bash
gx auth login --name "work-laptop"
```

Log out with:

```bash
gx auth logout
```

## Initialize a repo

Run `gx init` once, from the repository you want GX to manage:

```text
$ gx init

Configured     gx identity as Ada Doc <ada@example.com>
Pre-push hook  ok: capture on git push
Claude hooks   ok: Stop/SessionEnd transcript capture
Session        30 days retention
MCP            ok: claude
AGENTS.md      ok: added GX workflow instructions

Next           git add <files> && gx commit -m "..."
```

Line by line:

- **gx identity** — the name and email recorded on GX revisions. Defaults to your Git identity; override with `gx init --name "..." --email "..."`.
- **Pre-push hook** — a Git pre-push hook, so plain `git push` also captures sessions and publishes GX metadata on the way out.
- **Claude hooks** — Claude Code `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks, so agent transcripts are captured as GX sessions.
- **Session retention** — captured sessions are kept locally for 30 days.
- **MCP** — registers the [GX MCP server](/docs/mcp) with supported agent CLIs found on the machine.
- **AGENTS.md** — offers to append GX workflow instructions so agents working in this repo use `gx commit` instead of `git commit`.

For scripts and agent sandboxes, `gx init -y` accepts all defaults and suppresses interactive prompts.

## Optional: bring your own model key

You do not need a model API key to use GX. The core workflow is fully deterministic, and once you sign in, AI features like `gx review` run through GX Cloud on your plan or free trial.

Set your own key only when you want GX to call a specific provider or model directly:

```bash
gx set key                                              # interactive: pick provider, paste key
gx set key --provider anthropic --key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"   # scripts
```

GX looks for an existing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment first, and stores a pasted key in `~/.gx/inference.json` (or `$GX_HOME/inference.json`). When both are available, your own key takes precedence over GX Cloud.

Paid pull request features (PR Summaries, `@gx` chat) always run through GX Cloud, never your local keys.

## First revision

After making changes, stage the files that belong together and record them:

```text
$ git add src/retry.js
$ gx commit -m "add retry helper with attempt limit"

Revision recorded
Message       add retry helper with attempt limit
Revision      qltmnmynnyzk
Commit        b694d3be
Stack         main
Provenance    absent
```

What happened:

- `git add` chose the scope — only `src/retry.js` is part of this revision. Use `git add -p` to select individual hunks.
- `gx commit` recorded the staged changes as a GX revision. Like `git commit`, it landed on the current branch and `HEAD` did not move.
- The revision is JJ-backed, so it stays editable through GX tools later — no interactive rebase needed.
- `Provenance: absent` means no captured coding session was linked. When an agent session is captured, GX matches it automatically and this shows the linked status instead.

If nothing is staged, `gx commit` refuses with exit code `2`:

```text
$ gx commit -m "nothing staged"
no staged changes; run git add first
```

Then publish:

```bash
gx status   # inspect first (alias: gxs)
git push    # the GX pre-push hook captures sessions and publishes metadata
```

`git push` pushes normal Git refs; with the GX hook installed, capture and cloud publish happen on the way out. You can also publish explicitly with `gx push`, which prints GitHub and review URLs when available.

## Build a stack

Pass `-b` to start a new branch for a line of work, then keep committing to grow the stack:

```text
$ git add src/backoff.js
$ gx commit -m "add exponential backoff helper" -b feature/retry-backoff

Revision recorded
Created branch feature/retry-backoff (from main)
Message       add exponential backoff helper
Revision      qlmmuyyyupkm
Commit        14c101a1
Stack         feature/retry-backoff

$ git add src/jitter.js
$ gx commit -m "add jitter to backoff delays"

Revision recorded
Message       add jitter to backoff delays
Revision      zlsrnukorkyz
Commit        ae0d5b62
Stack         feature/retry-backoff
```

`gx status` now shows one stack with two ordered revisions, newest first:

```text
$ gx status

demo-repo  ● retry-backoff

› ● retry-backoff  s1 · feature/retry-backoff · main · draft · ↑2
        ↑ zlsrnuk  add jitter to backoff delays  latest
        ↑ qlmmuyy  add exponential backoff helper
```

Reading the stack line: `s1` is a short alias you can use in commands, `feature/retry-backoff` is the Git branch it exports to, `main` is the base, `draft` means it has not been published, and `↑2` means two revisions are ahead of the remote.

## Agent workflow

Prefer MCP tools over asking agents to run the CLI directly. The expected save flow is:

1. Stage with `git add`
2. `gx_commit` — record the revision (agents can attach a task summary and the commands/tests they ran)
3. `gx_status` — inspect before publish
4. `gx_push` — publish ready stacks (or `git push` when the hook is enough)

Use `gx_sync` first when remote GitHub or GX state may have moved. Use `gx_generate` only to bulk-organize a large messy working copy.

See [MCP setup](/docs/mcp) for client registration and per-tool parameters.

## Optional: first-run demo

```bash
gx demo
```

Walks through how GX works in an interactive scratch session, without touching your repository.

# How it works

GX adds a context layer around your existing Git workflow. It captures what happened during coding sessions, attaches that context to reviewable revisions, and publishes normal Git branches and commits — so reviewers see the intent behind a change, not just the final diff.

## The problem

Git was built for humans typing commits one at a time. A commit stores a snapshot and a short message, and for human-paced work that is usually enough.

Agent-written code breaks two of Git's assumptions:

1. **The context that explains a change never makes it into the repo.** The prompt that asked for the change, the commands the agent ran, the tests it executed, the dead ends it backed out of — all of that lives in a session transcript that is gone by review time. The commit message is whatever one line survived.
2. **Review is now the bottleneck.** The cost of generating code is dropping toward zero, but teams still review line by line. When a pull request is one large undifferentiated diff with a thin message, the reviewer has to reconstruct intent from scratch.

## What GX captures

GX records work at three levels:

- **Sessions** — transcripts from coding agents (for example, Claude Code transcripts via `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks that `gx init` installs). Sessions are retained locally for 30 days and published alongside the code they produced.
- **Revisions** — each `gx commit` records the staged changes as one reviewable unit, down to individual [hunks](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Interactive-Staging) (a few changed lines, not whole files). GX links each revision to the session that produced it — automatically when it can match one, or explicitly when an agent declares it.
- **Agent self-reports** — through the [MCP tools](/docs/mcp), an agent can attach a task summary and the commands and tests it ran directly to the revision it is committing.

Because changes are stored as described hunks with linked sessions, GX can point reviewers at the parts that matter and let them skim the mechanical rest — instead of forcing a line-by-line read of everything.

## Stacks and revisions

You are likely used to the Git mental model of branches and commits. These work great until you need to edit a commit, rebase, or reorder work — then the tooling gets sharp.

- A **revision** is analogous to a commit, but it can be edited and updated after it is recorded. Revisions are JJ-backed, so amending one never requires an interactive rebase.
- A **stack** is analogous to a branch, but with metadata: an ordered line of revisions, their base, publish state, and remote sync status. Status output also calls a stack a **feature**.

Here is a stack as `gx status` shows it — two revisions built on `main`, not yet published:

```text
› ● retry-backoff  s1 · feature/retry-backoff · main · draft · ↑2
        ↑ zlsrnuk  add jitter to backoff delays  latest
        ↑ qlmmuyy  add exponential backoff helper
```

Each revision is separately reviewable, and the order tells the story of the work. Stacks also make stacked PRs natural: each stack exports to a branch, and dependent work stays in sequence instead of piling into one giant diff.

## Everything still exports to Git

GX maintains revisions and stacks locally. When you push — via `git push` with the GX pre-push hook, or `gx push` — GX publishes:

- normal Git **branches and commits**, so your Git log and GitHub stay standard;
- the linked **sessions and metadata** to GX Cloud as a review bundle.

Nothing about your repository becomes GX-specific. If you stopped using GX tomorrow, your branches and commits remain ordinary Git.

## Replace your git workflow

Instead of manually creating a branch and commit:

```bash
git checkout -b feature/my-change
git add .
git commit -m "update stuff"
git push
```

Start with:

```bash
git add <files>
gx commit -m "describe this revision"   # add -b feature/my-change for a new branch
gx status                               # alias: gxs
git push                                # or gx push
```

`gx commit` records staged work as a GX revision. `gx status` shows local stacks and remote state. `git push` (with the GX pre-push hook) or `gx push` publishes code plus session data and metadata to GitHub and GX Cloud.

For a large messy working copy, agents can still run `gx generate` to bulk-organize changes into smaller revisions, then inspect with `gx status` and push when ready.

## Where the context goes

The published review bundle powers the review surfaces:

- [PR Summaries](/docs/github) tell reviewers what changed, why, and which files deserve attention first.
- [`@gx` chat](/docs/github) answers questions inside the pull request, citing the sessions and diffs it used.
- [`gx review`](/docs/cli) runs a local review using the same captured context before you ever open a PR.

The recommended way to use GX with agents is through the [MCP server](/docs/mcp). That lets your coding tool record and publish work without touching the terminal.

# CLI

`gx` is the local CLI. It is open source and runs on your machine. It adds a quality and workflow layer around your existing repo instead of replacing GitHub.

GX still produces ordinary Git branches and commits as output. The difference is that GX models the work first as reviewable revisions inside ordered stacks, with captured session context attached.

## Core loop

```bash
git add <files>                        # choose the scope of the revision
gx commit -m "describe this revision"  # record it
gx status                              # inspect stacks (alias: gxs)
git push                               # GX pre-push hook captures sessions and publishes metadata
```

Or publish explicitly with `gx push` instead of `git push`.

## gx init

```bash
gx init
```

Prepares the current repository for GX: configures local identity, installs a Git pre-push hook, installs Claude Code transcript-capture hooks, registers the MCP server with supported agent CLIs, and offers to add GX workflow instructions to `AGENTS.md`.

Run it once per repository.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | user name to store in GX and JJ config (defaults to Git identity) |
| `--email <email>` | user email to store in GX and JJ config |
| `-y`, `--yes` | accept defaults and suppress prompts — use in scripts and agent sandboxes |

```text
$ gx init

Configured     gx identity as Ada Doc <ada@example.com>
Pre-push hook  ok: capture on git push
Claude hooks   ok: Stop/SessionEnd transcript capture
Session        30 days retention
MCP            ok: claude
AGENTS.md      ok: added GX workflow instructions

Next           git add <files> && gx commit -m "..."
```

## gx commit

```bash
git add <files>    # or git add -p to pick hunks
gx commit -m "describe this revision"
```

Records **staged** Git changes as a GX revision. Like `git commit`, the revision lands on the current branch and `HEAD` does not move. The revision is JJ-backed, so it stays editable through GX tools later.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-m`, `--message <msg>` | commit message (required) |
| `-b`, `--branch <name>` | create this branch at `HEAD` and record the revision onto it |
| `--context-file <path>` | JSON file with agent-declared provenance (see below) |
| `--json` | print machine-readable JSON (repo, change, stack, provenance status) |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` general error, `2` no staged changes.

```text
$ gx commit -m "add exponential backoff helper" -b feature/retry-backoff

Revision recorded
Created branch feature/retry-backoff (from main)
Message       add exponential backoff helper
Revision      qlmmuyyyupkm
Commit        14c101a1
Stack         feature/retry-backoff
Provenance    absent
```

`Revision` is the stable GX change id; `Commit` is the Git commit it exported. `Provenance` reports session linkage: `absent` when no captured session matched, or a linked status when GX matched a captured session or one was attached explicitly (agents attach sessions through [MCP `gx_commit`](/docs/mcp)).

Some `git commit` flags are intentionally rejected, with the replacement in the error message:

- `gx commit -a` — not supported; stage with `git add` first, so the revision scope is explicit.
- `gx commit --amend` — not supported; use `gx edit <rev>` to modify a recorded revision.
- `gx commit -F <file>` — not supported yet; pass the message with `-m`.
- `gx commit <path>` — path arguments are rejected; choose scope with `git add` or `git add -p`.

### Agent-declared provenance

`--context-file` attaches a self-report to the revision. All fields are optional:

```json
{
  "task_summary": "Add retry/backoff utilities requested in TICKET-482",
  "commands_run": ["bun test retry.test.js"],
  "tests_run": ["bun test"]
}
```

```bash
gx commit -m "retry: honor attempt limit" --context-file context.json
```

This is how a coding agent records *what it did* alongside *what changed*. Reviewers see the summary and the tests that ran next to the diff. MCP's `gx_commit` tool exposes these as first-class parameters, so agents rarely need to write the file themselves.

## gx status

```bash
gx status        # alias: gxs
```

Shows unstaged changes, local stacks (features), their revisions, and remote sync status.

```text
$ gx status

demo-repo  ● retry-backoff

› ● retry-backoff  s1 · feature/retry-backoff · main · draft · ↑2
        ↑ zlsrnuk  add jitter to backoff delays  latest
        ↑ qlmmuyy  add exponential backoff helper
```

Reading the stack header, left to right: stack name, `s1` short alias (usable in commands like `gx push s1`), the Git branch it exports to, the base branch, publish state (`draft` until pushed), and `↑2` — two revisions ahead of the remote.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | machine-readable stack summary |
| `--agent` | stable, line-oriented text for agents (see below) |
| `--all` | list all changed files in the git working tree sections |
| `-i`, `--interactive` | open the interactive status browser |

`--agent` is the format coding agents should parse when not using MCP — one `key=value` line per stack and revision:

```text
$ gx status --agent
next: "git add"
repo=demo-repo stacks=1 current=retry-backoff
stack name=retry-backoff alias=s1 ref=feature/retry-backoff base=main status=draft changes=2 published=0/2 sync=local current=true
revision id=qlmmuyyyupkm message="add exponential backoff helper" status=draft commit=14c101a1
revision id=zlsrnukorkyz message="add jitter to backoff delays" status=draft commit=ae0d5b62
```

### Subcommands

```bash
gx status list                     # all non-merged GX features (--json, --agent)
gx status edit <revision>          # reopen a recorded revision to keep working on it
gx status diff <revision-or-stack> # show the JJ diff for a revision or stack
```

```text
$ gx status diff zlsrnukorkyz
Added regular file jitter.js:
        1: export function jitter(ms) {
        2:   return ms / 2 + Math.random() * (ms / 2);
        3: }
```

## gx review

```bash
gx review                                 # alias: gxr
gx review "check auth rollback risks"
```

Reviews local changes using codebase context, captured sessions, review resources, and optional prompt guidance. Findings are printed as markdown and recorded to review history so future reviews can retrieve previous decisions.

AI reviewers are optional and resolve credentials in this order: your own key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `gx set key`), then GX Cloud when you are signed in (on your plan or free trial), then deterministic checks only — the review always completes, with a warning naming what was unavailable.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[prompt]` | optional positional prompt to steer the review |
| `--scope <scope>` | focused review scope: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `--focus <path>` | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `--deep` | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `--verbose` | include repo facts, docs, and changed files in the output |

Examples:

```bash
gx review --scope security                  # security-focused pass over the current changes
gx review --focus src/auth --deep           # deep review of just the auth directory
gx review "did we break the retry contract?"
```

## gx push

```bash
gx push              # push the current stack, like git push
gx push s1           # push a specific stack by name or alias
gx push --all        # push every accepted stack
```

Publishes stacks: normal Git branches and commits, linked sessions, and review metadata. Prints branch, GitHub push status, PR status/URL, and an Actions link when available. When an edited revision rewrites a stack, GX uses a guarded force-push with lease.

Like `git push`, the default is only the current stack — pushing everything requires the explicit `--all` so GX never publishes branches you did not ask to share.

With the pre-push hook from `gx init`, plain `git push` also triggers capture and cloud publish for the pushed refs.

## gx sync

```bash
gx sync              # sync the default remote
gx sync upstream     # sync a specific remote
```

Fetches remote Git and GX state before committing or pushing: updates remote bookmarks, catches up local state to merged/closed PRs, prunes stacks whose PRs reached a terminal state, and drains any queued cloud uploads.

Use it when GitHub moved (a branch was merged or closed), or when `gx push` reports remote divergence.

## gx auth

```bash
gx auth login                     # sign in through GitHub
gx auth login --name "work-mbp"   # set the machine name shown in the console
gx auth status                    # show current auth state (--json for scripts)
gx auth logout
```

Signs the CLI into GX Cloud through GitHub. Signed-in devices appear in the web app with machine name, GX version, last-used time, and session expiry.

## gx set key

```bash
gx set key                                            # interactive: pick provider, paste key
gx set key --provider anthropic --key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Optional — GX works without a key, and signed-in users get AI features through GX Cloud. Set one when you want GX to call a specific provider or model directly. Stores the key in `~/.gx/inference.json` (or `$GX_HOME/inference.json`); an existing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment is preferred when present. Providers: `anthropic`, `openai`.

## gx doctor

```bash
gx doctor          # diagnose capture, hooks, Codex routing, stale stacks
gx doctor --fix    # apply safe repairs
gx doctor --json   # machine-readable report
```

Checks local GX setup and workflow state: session capture health, Codex config routing, stacks whose base ref went missing, and stale stacks. `--fix` cleans up stale stacks, repairs missing base refs, and rewires configuration where it is safe to do so.

## gx report

```bash
gx report          # --json for the report id/URL
```

Uploads recent GX logs to support and prints a report ID and URL. Use it when something misbehaves and you want the team to see what happened. Needs GX Cloud: use a released install and `gx auth login`.

## gx version

```bash
gx version
gx version --json   # machine-readable build metadata
```

## gx demo

```bash
gx demo
```

Interactive first-run walkthrough in a scratch session — safe to run anywhere; it does not touch your repository.

## Shortcuts

The CLI installer installs:

```bash
gxs   # gx status
gxr   # gx review
```

They are symlinks to the same `gx` binary.

## Bulk organize (advanced)

`gx generate` is hidden from `gx --help`. Use it when you want GX to organize a large working copy into smaller revisions automatically:

```bash
gx generate
gx status
gx push
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[filesets...]` | limit generation to these changed files or directories |
| `--exclude <path>` | exclude a changed file or directory; may be repeated |
| `--intent <text>` | intent prefix attached to generated revisions |
| `--json` | machine-readable plan and result |
| `--raw` | show full generate diagnostics in human output |

For most day-to-day work, prefer `git add` + `gx commit` — explicit scope beats bulk organization when you already know what belongs together.

## Surgery commands (advanced)

Hidden commands for explicit repair work, not the default flow:

```bash
gx edit            # pick a recorded revision to reopen and keep working on
gx edit <rev>      # reopen a specific revision
gx base            # show the GX authoring base and current ref
gx base --set main # return the authoring base to the default branch
```

```text
$ gx base
GX base
Base          main
Current       feature/retry-backoff
On base       no

Return        gx base --set main
```

## Diagnostics (advanced)

Hidden utility commands for capture and support:

```bash
gx capture sync         # force a session capture sync
gx ops diagnose doctor  # deeper ops diagnosis surface
```

Prefer the public `gx doctor` and `gx report` unless you need the deeper ops surface.

# MCP Setup

The GX MCP server is installed with the CLI. It shells out to your local `gx` binary, so repo state stays on your machine.

## Install GX first

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
```

The installer places `gx-mcp` next to `gx` in `~/.local/bin`.

If a repo is not initialized, MCP runs `gx init` non-interactively before repository tools continue — using Git identity when available, or the `GX_MCP_INIT_NAME` / `GX_MCP_INIT_EMAIL` environment variables.

## Register the MCP server

The released CLI installs a stdio MCP server at `~/.local/bin/gx-mcp`. Register that binary with each agent you use. `gx init` also registers supported clients automatically when it finds them.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add gx -- env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

### Cursor

```bash
cursor mcp add gx -- env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

### Codex CLI and Codex app

For Codex CLI:

```bash
codex mcp add gx --env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx -- $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

Codex CLI and the Codex app both read MCP servers from `~/.codex/config.toml`. You can also add the server manually with absolute paths:

```toml
[mcp_servers.gx]
command = "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx-mcp"

[mcp_servers.gx.env]
GX_BINARY = "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx"
```

On Linux, use `/home/YOU/.local/bin/gx-mcp` and `/home/YOU/.local/bin/gx`.

### Other MCP clients

Other clients use the same stdio command shape:

```bash
env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

## Tools

| Tool | CLI command | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gx_commit` | `gx commit -m "..."` | Record staged Git changes as a GX revision (**default save**) |
| `gx_status` | `gx status --json` | Inspect unstaged work, features, revisions, and remote state |
| `gx_push` | `gx push [stack]` | Publish stacks, sessions, and metadata |
| `gx_sync` | `gx sync` | Reflect remote GitHub and GX state locally |
| `gx_review` | `gx review [prompt]` | Review using local and cloud context |
| `gx_generate` | `gx generate --json` | Bulk-organize a large working copy (secondary) |
| `gx_set_base` | `gx base --set <default>` | Return authoring base to the repo default branch |

All tools accept an optional `cwd` (repository working directory; defaults to the MCP server process cwd). Long-running tools (`gx_push`, `gx_sync`, `gx_review`, `gx_generate`) allow up to 5 minutes.

### gx_commit

The default save verb. Stage files with `git add` first.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string (required) | commit message for the staged revision |
| `branch` | string | create this branch at `HEAD` and record onto it; default: current branch |
| `task_summary` | string | agent-declared summary of the work being committed |
| `commands_run` | string[] | shell commands the agent ran while doing this work |
| `tests_run` | string[] | test commands the agent ran |
| `session_id` | string | captured GX session id to attach as provenance |

The provenance fields are the reason to prefer `gx_commit` over shelling out: they attach *what the agent did* to the revision, and reviewers see it next to the diff.

```json
{
  "message": "retry: honor attempt limit",
  "task_summary": "Add retry/backoff utilities requested in TICKET-482",
  "commands_run": ["bun test retry.test.js"],
  "tests_run": ["bun test"]
}
```

### gx_status

Read-only. Returns the `gx status --json` stack summary: unstaged files, features, revisions, publish counts, and remote sync state. Optional `show_all` includes hidden compatibility state.

### gx_push

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stack` | string | stack/feature name to push; omit to push the current stack, like `git push` |
| `all` | boolean | push every accepted stack instead of only the current one |

If the result reports remote divergence, run `gx_sync` and retry the push for that stack.

### gx_sync

Optional `remote` selects a specific remote. Run it before committing or pushing when remote GitHub merges may have landed.

### gx_review

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | reviewer prompt, e.g. `"check auth rollback risks"` |
| `scope` | enum | `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `focus` | string | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `deep` | boolean | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `verbose` | boolean | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |

### gx_generate

Bulk organizer for a large messy working copy — secondary to `gx_commit`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | string | intent prefix for generated revisions |
| `filesets` | string[] | changed files or directories to include |
| `exclude` | string[] | changed files or directories to exclude |
| `session_id` / `session_ids` | string / string[] | captured GX session ids to include as provenance |

`gx_generate` runs in a session-isolated JJ workspace under `$GX_HOME/workspaces/...` so concurrent MCP sessions do not generate each other's dirty checkout. It requires a session id: pass `session_id` / `session_ids`, or set `GX_SESSION_ID` / `GX_SESSION_IDS` in the server environment.

### gx_set_base

Returns the GX authoring base to the repository default branch. It intentionally does not accept an arbitrary branch target.

## Agent workflow

When a user says "save work", "save using gx", or "save with gx", run:

1. Stage with `git add` (choose the scope — one logical change per revision)
2. `gx_commit` with a message and, when available, `task_summary` / `commands_run` / `tests_run`
3. `gx_status` — inspect before publish
4. `gx_push` for ready stacks (unless they ask to keep work local)

Use `gx_sync` first when remote merges may have landed. Use `gx_generate` only for bulk organization of large working copies.

A typical save sequence, as tool calls:

```jsonc
// 1. after: git add src/backoff.js
{ "tool": "gx_commit", "arguments": {
  "message": "add exponential backoff helper",
  "branch": "feature/retry-backoff",
  "task_summary": "Backoff helper for the retry work in TICKET-482",
  "tests_run": ["bun test"]
} }

// 2. verify the stack looks right
{ "tool": "gx_status", "arguments": {} }

// 3. publish the current stack
{ "tool": "gx_push", "arguments": {} }
```

GX PR summaries are posted for PRs published or adopted through GX push. A PR created only with the GitHub UI will not get a GX summary until that branch is pushed through GX.

## AGENTS.md instructions

`gx init` offers to append these instructions to your repo's `AGENTS.md`, so agents that read repo instructions use GX by default. If you skipped that step, add them manually:

```markdown
Version control: use GX, not `git commit`.

Default flow:
- Run `git add` to stage the files for this revision.
- Run `gx commit` (or MCP `gx_commit`) to record staged work as a GX revision.
- Run `gx status` to inspect staged files, local features/revisions, and remote state.
- Run `gx push` to push code changes, sessions, and GX metadata to GitHub/origin
  and GX Cloud. Plain `git push` also works when the GX pre-push hook is installed.

Use GX MCP first: `gx_sync`, `gx_status`, then `gx_commit` / `gx_push`.
If MCP is unavailable, use the CLI fallback: `git add`, `gx commit`, `gx status`, then `git push`.

Use hidden utility commands such as `gx base` or `gx edit` only for explicit
surgery or user-directed repair.

Use `gx generate` only for bulk organization of large working copies.
```

# Interact with GX in GitHub PRs

GX adds paid review features inside GitHub pull requests.

The CLI can record and publish stacks locally for free. GitHub PR Summaries and `@gx` chat run through GX Cloud and require the paid PR feature set (or an active free trial).

## Prerequisites

1. Sign in with `gx auth login`.
2. Install the GX GitHub App on the repository so GX can post comments and read PR context.
3. Point the GitHub App webhook at the GX Cloud API:

```text
https://api.gx.run/github/webhook
```

4. Publish work through GX (`gx push`, or `git push` with the GX pre-push hook). A PR created only in the GitHub UI will not get a GX summary until that branch is pushed through GX with capture metadata present.

## PR Summaries

GX can post a PR Summary comment on a GitHub pull request.

The summary is intentionally short. It should tell reviewers:

- what changed
- why it changed
- which files deserve attention first
- which files are mechanical or safe to skim
- what session or agent context is relevant

The goal is to point reviewers to the important parts of the change instead of forcing them to read every line with no context.

### When summaries are generated

GX posts summaries from these paths:

- **GitHub webhook** — on `pull_request` `opened` / `synchronize`, when the branch already has a published GX event
- **After publish** — when `gx push` (or the publish hook path) has a PR number and the GitHub App is installed

The [`POST /v1/summaries/generate`](/docs/reference/api) API stores a summary in GX Cloud. It does **not** post the comment to GitHub by itself.

### Trial and paid access

Orgs on the free plan get PR Summaries during a free trial window (default 7 days from org creation, or the entitlement returned by GX Cloud). After the trial ends, summaries require a paid plan. When quota blocks a summary, GX can post an upgrade comment on the PR instead.

## Chat with `@gx`

Mention `@gx` in a PR comment to ask questions about the pull request.

Ask for orientation:

```text
@gx summarize this PR for someone reviewing it cold
@gx which files should I review first?
@gx what is safe to skim?
```

Ask about a specific part of the diff:

```text
@gx explain the auth callback changes
@gx why did the migration file change?
@gx what does this new background job do?
```

Ask for risk or follow-up review:

```text
@gx what is the highest-risk change in this PR?
@gx are there missing tests?
@gx is this related to the previous retry bug?
```

GX answers from available review sources and cites the sources it used. Because published revisions carry session provenance, `@gx` can answer "why" questions — what the author asked for, which commands and tests ran — that a plain diff cannot.

### Override learned rules

You can use `@gx` to retire a learned rule:

```text
@gx skip rule never use var
@gx do not enforce this migration naming rule
```

When a matching active rule exists, GX retires it and records the override. Rule overrides require GitHub **write**, **maintain**, or **admin** permission on the repository. Collaborators without write access are denied.

## Data sources

GX answers from the current PR first: the published GX revision diffs, changed hunks, file paths, PR comments, and the latest PR Summary.

When available, GX can also use captured coding-session context, indexed codebase context, previous findings, learned rules, and git blame history. Current PR changes remain the source of truth for what changed.

## GitHub App

To post summaries and replies, GX needs installation-scoped access for the repository. The local CLI can still record and push branches without the paid PR feature set. The paid features are the GitHub-hosted review layer: PR Summaries, `@gx` chat, and cloud-backed review context.

# Troubleshooting

Start with the built-in doctor:

```bash
gx doctor          # diagnose capture, hooks, Codex routing, stale stacks
gx doctor --fix    # apply safe repairs automatically
```

If something still misbehaves, `gx report` uploads recent GX logs to support and prints a report ID you can share.

## Common errors

### `no staged changes; run git add first`

`gx commit` records **staged** changes only, and exits with code `2` when the index is empty.

```bash
git add <files>     # or git add -p to select hunks
gx commit -m "describe this revision"
```

Agents checking exit codes: `0` success, `1` general error, `2` nothing staged.

### `Run gx init first.`

The repository has no GX identity yet. Initialize it once:

```bash
gx init        # interactive
gx init -y     # accept defaults, for scripts and agent sandboxes
```

### `gx commit -a is not supported`

Deliberate. GX wants the revision scope to be explicit, so `-a`, `--amend`, and `-F` are rejected with the replacement in the message:

- instead of `-a`: stage with `git add` first
- instead of `--amend`: `gx edit <rev>` reopens a recorded revision
- instead of `-F file`: pass the message with `-m`

### Push reports remote divergence

The remote moved since your last sync — a branch was merged, closed, or force-pushed. Reflect remote state locally, then retry:

```bash
gx sync
gx push
```

`gx sync` also prunes stacks whose PRs were merged or closed, so status stops showing stale work.

### `Could not upload GX review context ... GX Cloud is not configured`

The push of Git refs succeeded, but the session/metadata upload was skipped because the CLI has no cloud endpoint. Released installs have the endpoint baked in, so this usually means a from-source build — set `GX_CLOUD_URL` or reinstall the released CLI:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth status || gx auth login
```

Local remote metadata is still recorded, so nothing is lost. Queued uploads are drained on the next successful `gx sync` or `gx push`.

### `gx-mcp not found; install GX CLI package first`

`gx init` tried to register the MCP server but could not find the `gx-mcp` binary. Reinstall the CLI package, which places both binaries in `~/.local/bin`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
```

Then re-run `gx init`, or register manually per [MCP setup](/docs/mcp).

### No PR Summary appeared on my pull request

Check, in order:

1. The branch was pushed **through GX** — `gx push`, or `git push` with the GX pre-push hook installed. A PR created only in the GitHub UI has no capture metadata.
2. The GX GitHub App is installed on the repository, with the webhook pointed at `https://api.gx.run/github/webhook`.
3. Your org's trial window or paid plan is active — when quota blocks a summary, GX posts an upgrade comment instead. See [Pull Requests](/docs/github).

### Sessions are not being captured

`gx init` installs the capture hooks (Git pre-push, Claude Code `Stop`/`SessionEnd`). Verify and repair:

```bash
gx doctor          # shows capture and hook state
gx doctor --fix
gx capture sync    # advanced: force a capture sync
```

Captured sessions are retained locally for 30 days.

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GX_HOME` | override GX's state directory (default `~/.gx`) — inference key, capture data, workspaces |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | model credentials for local inference; `gx set key` stores one persistently |
| `GX_BINARY` | path to the `gx` binary the MCP server should run |
| `GX_MCP_INIT_NAME` / `GX_MCP_INIT_EMAIL` | identity for MCP's non-interactive `gx init` |
| `GX_SESSION_ID` / `GX_SESSION_IDS` | session ids for MCP `gx_generate` workspace isolation |

## Uninstall

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/gx ~/.local/bin/gxr ~/.local/bin/gxs ~/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

This removes the installed binaries only. Local GX data remains in `~/.gx`; delete that directory too if you want a clean slate. Your Git repositories are untouched — everything GX published is ordinary Git.

## Send logs to support

```bash
gx report
```

Uploads recent GX logs (requires `gx auth login`) and prints a report ID and URL to share with the team.

# API

GX Cloud APIs use bearer-token authentication.

```bash
export GX_API_URL="https://api.gx.run"
```

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | API and database reachability |
| `GET /v1/auth/me` | inspect the authenticated caller |
| `POST /v1/publish` | publish a GX review bundle (what `gx push` sends) |
| `GET /bookmarks` | list bookmark metadata for sync and review |
| `GET /v1/review/context` | review context for a repo/ref range |
| `GET /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId` (+ `/plan`, `/decision`) | Console review experience |
| `POST /v1/summaries/generate` | generate and store a PR Summary |
| `POST /github/webhook` | GitHub App webhook (PR Summaries, `@gx` chat) |
| `POST /v1/extracts` | ingest hunk links and push metadata |
| `POST /v1/sessions` | ingest raw captured session content |
| `GET /v1/activity` | recent summaries, sessions, learned rules |
| `POST /v1/code-review-history/record` / `/search` | record and search review findings |
| `POST /v1/reported-logs` | upload CLI logs for support |
| `POST /gx/openai/responses` / `/chat-completions` | OpenAI proxy through GX Cloud |

## Authentication

`requireAuth` accepts these modes:

### GitHub token

For most user-facing integrations:

```bash
gh auth status || gh auth login
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"
```

If you need to refresh scopes for private repositories:

```bash
gh auth refresh -s read:user -s repo
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"
```

Attach the token:

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

GX validates GitHub tokens against the GitHub user API and maps the caller to `github:<id>`. You can optionally add `X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID`; otherwise GX resolves a default org.

### CLI session token

After `gx auth login`, the CLI can use a `gxcs_*` session token. The API verifies it through Convex (`CONVEX_SITE_URL` must be configured on the server).

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GX_CLI_SESSION_TOKEN"
```

### Console service key

The Console BFF authenticates with the shared cloud API key and impersonates a user:

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GX_CLOUD_API_KEY" \
-H "X-User-Id: $USER_ID" \
-H "X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID"
```

## GET /health

Check that the API and database are reachable.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/health"
```

## GET /v1/auth/me

Inspect the authenticated user, org, token label, CLI session, and machine when available.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

With an explicit org:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID"
```

Response fields include `org_id`, `user_id`, `token_label`, and optional GitHub/session machine fields.

## POST /v1/publish

Publish a GX review bundle. This is what `gx push` (and the publish path used after Git push with the GX hook) sends after it has produced Git branches, commits, sessions, and review metadata.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/publish" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "event": "gx.pr",
    "created_at": 1760000000000,
    "gx_version": "0.0.0",
    "repo": {
      "root_path": "/repo",
      "backend": "jj",
      "remote_url": "https://github.com/org/repo.git"
    },
    "push": {
      "branch_name": "feature/example",
      "head_commit_id": "abc123",
      "github_pull_request_url": "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123"
    },
    "stack": [],
    "sessions": []
  }'
```

The server stores the publish event, upserts a bookmark, indexes artifacts when configured, and returns review/bookmark metadata. When a PR number is present and the GitHub App is installed, publish may also post a missing PR Summary.

Without `event: "gx.pr"`, the same route accepts a lighter **registration-only** payload (`repo_full_name`, `branch_name`, `head_commit_id`, …) to upsert bookmark metadata.

## GET /bookmarks

List bookmark metadata for sync and review surfaces, newest first.

Query parameters: `merge_status` (`open`, `merged`, or `closed`; any other value is a `400`) and `repo_full_name`. Both optional.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/bookmarks?merge_status=open" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

Filter to one repository:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/bookmarks?repo_full_name=org/repo&merge_status=open" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

Response: an array of bookmarks.

```json
[
  {
    "id": "bm_123",
    "repo_full_name": "org/repo",
    "branch_name": "feature/retry-backoff",
    "title": "Add retry/backoff utilities",
    "revision": 3,
    "head_commit_id": "ae0d5b62...",
    "remote_head_sha": "ae0d5b62...",
    "merge_status": "open",
    "updated_at_ms": 1760000000000
  }
]
```

## GET /v1/review/context

Fetch review context for a repo/ref range. The response can include rules, collision hints, hunk links, and indexed snippets.

```bash
curl --get "$GX_API_URL/v1/review/context" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "repoRoot=/repo" \
  --data-urlencode "base=main" \
  --data-urlencode "head=HEAD"
```

## Console review experience

These routes power the Console review UI. They require auth like other `/v1` routes.

### GET /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId

Load the full review experience for a bookmark (plan, usage, changes, summary, activity).

### POST /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId/plan

Generate or regenerate a review plan for the bookmark.

### POST /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId/decision

Record an approve/merge decision. Passing `merged: true` updates bookmark `merge_status`.

## POST /v1/summaries/generate

Generate a PR Summary for a bookmark or event and **store it in GX Cloud**. This endpoint does not post the comment to GitHub; GitHub posting is driven by the webhook and publish paths. See [GitHub PRs](/docs/github).

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/summaries/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bookmarkId":"..."}'
```

Or generate from an event:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/summaries/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"eventId":"..."}'
```

PR Summary and GitHub PR chat features are paid GX Cloud features (with a free-trial window).

## POST /github/webhook

GitHub App webhook endpoint for PR Summaries and `@gx` chat.

```text
POST https://api.gx.run/github/webhook
```

Authenticated with `X-Hub-Signature-256`, not a bearer token. Configure this URL on the GitHub App.

## POST /v1/extracts

Ingest hunk links and push metadata.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/extracts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoRoot": "/repo",
    "refRange": "main..HEAD",
    "headCommit": "abc123",
    "gxVersion": "0.0.0",
    "hunkLinks": [
      {
        "hunkID": "src/app.ts:10-20",
        "file": "src/app.ts",
        "lineStart": 10,
        "lineEnd": 20,
        "tier": 1,
        "confidence": 0.91,
        "authorship": "agent",
        "tool": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /v1/sessions

Ingest raw captured session content.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "sessionId": "session-123",
    "tool": "codex",
    "model": "gpt-5",
    "content": "redacted transcript text",
    "capturedAtMs": 1760000000000
  }'
```

## GET /v1/activity

Read recent summaries, sessions, and learned rules. `limit` accepts 1–100 (default 20); page with the returned `nextCursor`.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/activity?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

With pagination:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/activity?limit=20&cursor=$CURSOR" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

Response shape: `{ items, limit, nextCursor }`.

## POST /v1/code-review-history/record

Record review findings so future reviews can retrieve previous decisions and patterns.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/code-review-history/record" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoFullName": "org/repo",
    "repoRootPath": "/repo",
    "branchName": "feature/example",
    "headCommitId": "abc123",
    "sourceKind": "manual",
    "prompt": "review auth changes",
    "summaryText": "Auth review completed",
    "findings": [
      {
        "title": "Missing validation",
        "summary": "The handler accepts an unchecked token.",
        "filePath": "src/auth.ts",
        "lineStart": 42,
        "severity": "medium",
        "confidence": 0.8
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /v1/code-review-history/search

Search prior review findings for a repo.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/code-review-history/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoFullName": "org/repo",
    "query": "auth validation",
    "filePaths": ["src/auth.ts"],
    "limit": 5
  }'
```

## POST /v1/reported-logs

Upload reported CLI logs for support.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/reported-logs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "gx_version": "0.0.0",
    "os": "darwin",
    "arch": "arm64",
    "repo_root": "/repo",
    "repo_full_name": "org/repo",
    "error": "publish failed",
    "logs": [
      {
        "path": "publish.log",
        "content": "redacted log content"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /gx/openai/responses

Proxy a valid OpenAI Responses API request through GX Cloud.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/gx/openai/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5",
    "instructions": "Be concise.",
    "input": "Summarize this change."
  }'
```

## POST /gx/openai/chat-completions

Proxy a valid OpenAI Chat Completions request through GX Cloud.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/gx/openai/chat-completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Summarize this change." }
    ]
  }'
```
